kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the printed tables — 4 patterns (the abrupt-withdrawal adrenal crisis, the six-link gynecomastia list, the SSRI/carbamazepine SIADH with urine-osmolality routing, the D2-blockade hyperprolactinemia presentation), 4 traps (lithium's DI-vs-SIADH opposite water arrows, amiodarone/lithium in both thyroid rows, androgen-cut vs estrogen-cut sex-steroid rows, drug-withdrawal secondary insufficiency vs primary Addison), 3 pivots (the axis+direction routing, the urine-osmolality tiebreaker, the on-drug hyperglycemia vs off-drug crisis timing), 8 recall cards — the whole exam layer is built on the endocrine table per the production rationale.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the table's facts only; the attack structure, the distractor designs, and the axis-routing protocol are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The four-axis reading protocol (NAME THE AXIS: HPA / sex-steroid / thyroid / water-glucose → NAME THE DIRECTION: suppressed vs stimulated, blocked vs enhanced, androgen-off vs estrogen-off → READ THE PRESENTATION the row predicts → MATCH THE CAUSAL-AGENT LIST using First Aid's own red keys), plus the observation that the same drug prints in multiple rows (lithium ×3, amiodarone ×2, glucocorticoids ×2, SSRIs across BOTH tables) so the axis+direction — never the drug name — is the answer key.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the rows as parallel table cells and never asks the learner to route a stem through axis → direction → presentation; the protocol and the double-appearance analysis are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + blocks[2] the steps block + blocks[3] the compare block + the registry visual's four-lane zone

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (ROUTE THE REACTION TO ITS AXIS / THE ADRENAL SLEEPS — TAPER, DON'T STOP / NO ANDROGEN SIGNAL, NEW BREAST TISSUE / ADH DOWN DILUTES, ADH UP DROWNS). No mnemonic prints in the page's margins; First Aid's own red in-cell mnemonic text (endocrine: 'The people need High glucose' · 'I am lethargic' · 'Can’t Concentrate Serum Sodium'; GI: 'I referred patient serum (AST, ALT) for hepatitis' · 'Drugs generate a violent abdominal distress' · 'Pills Not beneficial for food tube') is carried ATTRIBUTED inside the verbatim tables and is NOT counted among the four KYP codes.
kypExtensions.rationale: No margin mnemonic prints anywhere on pdf 270 (pdfimages + VLM census, staging-ph23/vlm-census.txt); the four ALL-CAPS codes are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + blocks[5] the memory callout + the visual's lane footers

kypExtensions.summary: The transplant-patient prednisone-withdrawal miniCase — which mechanism best explains the crisis — with the correct answer routing the printed row (chronic exogenous glucocorticoid → HPA suppression → abrupt withdrawal → adrenal crisis, secondary pattern: no hyperpigmentation, normal potassium) and distractors inventing gland destruction, swapping in tacrolimus (a real drug on the same page but in the hyperglycemia row), and borrowing the SIADH row whose printed list does not contain glucocorticoids.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the row as two cells and never dissects it against distractor mechanisms; the vignette, the four options, and the reasoning are KYP's design.

kypExtensions.summary: The five DrugCards (chronic exogenous glucocorticoids, spironolactone, amiodarone, lithium, carbamazepine + the SIADH trio) — one card per endocrine-axis anchor, each cell traceable to the printed rows (the GI table's drugs are NOT carded; its eight rows live verbatim in the table block and the visual strip, per the whole-page ownership).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source organizes the pharmacology as tables, not as drug cards; the card layer is a KYP presentation of the same printed facts.
